## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Bhikkhunupassaya Sikkhāpada* (Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 23) is the twenty-third rule in the *pācittiya* section of the Theravāda Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga [SuttaCentral]. It stipulates that a Buddhist monk who goes to a nuns' dwelling place (*bhikkhunūpassaya*) to exhort or teach them commits an offense requiring confession (*pācittiya*) [SuttaCentral]. The background narrative involves modest monks objecting to and complaining about monks who proceed to the nuns' quarters to instruct them [Horner 1952]. The text has been translated into English by Bhikkhu Brahmali on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral].

Full parallels are preserved across multiple early Buddhist monastic traditions, including the Pali *Bhikkhupātimokkha* and *Parivāra*, the Mahīśāsaka Vibhaṅga and Prātimokkha traditions in Chinese, the Mahāsāṅghika Vibhaṅga and Prātimokkha (Chinese and Sanskrit), the Lokottaravāda Sanskrit Bhikṣu-prātimokkha, the Kāśyapīya Prātimokkha in Chinese, and the Chinese translation of the *Upāliparipṛcchā* [SuttaCentral]. In DharmaNexus textual matching, this rule shares extensive internal Vinaya formulary with 125 other Pali texts—most prominently the *Bhesajjakkhandhaka* (Kd 6), the *Bhikkhunikkhandhaka* (Kd 20), the *Mahākhandhaka* (Kd 1), and related Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga pācittiya rules (such as Pc 27, Pc 46, Pc 57, and Pc 77)—as well as computational cross-language alignments with the Tibetan translation of the *Vinayakṣudrakavastu* (D0006-2) [DharmaNexus].
